brief: Decides whether to believe a SAML assertion posted back by a single trusted identity provider, and says why when it refuses.
detail: The signature check and the anti-wrapping guarantee belong to the engine, which returns claims read only from the signed bytes. This class adds the judgement that depends on your configuration: the issuer must be the trusted identity provider, the audience must be this provider's entity id, the validity window must contain the moment of judgement (with a clock-skew allowance, 120 seconds by default), and an assertion already accepted is refused as a replay. Every refusal returns a reason and is noted in the refusal record. Trust is set with raw key parts, a certificate, or the identity provider's metadata document. Known limits today: the sign-in request (AuthnRequest, AuthnRequestAt) writes its values into attributes without XML escaping and stamps IssueInstant with the clock in milliseconds, and a consumed subject comes back still XML-escaped.
